title: SIU clears officers in Taresh Bobby Ramroop's death from North York highrise
subtitle: The tragedy resurfaced criticisms on the preparedness of emergency services in handling individuals in crisis.
article: The Special Investigations Unit (SIU) said it will not lay charges on the police officers who were present when Taresh Bobby Ramroop's fell to his death from a highrise in North York last October.

A press release published on Thursday said that Joseph Martino, director of the SIU, said he found "no reasonable grounds" to believe that a Toronto police officer committed a criminal offence on Oct. 13, 2022.

The SIU said in an initial press release that Toronto police officers were called at around 4:30 p.m. to an apartment on Jane Street and Finch Avenue West after a man had been reportedly throwing objects from a balcony .
The statement said that three officers tried to negotiate with him. Another three officers from the Emergency Task Force joined them from an adjacent apartment.
"In the course of negotiations, the man fell from the apartment window to the ground below," the SIU said. He was pronounced dead at the scene.
The tragedy awakened a wave of criticisms from family and the community regarding the preparedness of emergency services to help individuals in crisis.

Days following his death, Ramroop's family questioned the number of officers quoted in the SIU press release, and demanded the Toronto police be abolished and replaced with a more "caring" emergency response, as well as the names of the officers involved and any footage be released.
A mobile crisis intervention team (MCIT) was not deployed at the time.
A candlelight vigil was held on Nov. 1 for Ramroop, who would have been celebrating his 33rd birthday that day.
